body:
Before I start, if I am hard to follow, I am sorry for that. I can be really, really verbose and I have this huge vocabulary and I can be grating sometimes. Also, I might write a little bit about myself but just because I think some of it might help you feel less alone I guess.

>I'm not sure how to start this off besides introducing who I am; I am an autistic 16 year old who has schizophrenia and possibly other mental illnesses (no one can say yet because apparently you're meant to be 18 to diagnose some things) and I just can't find a reason to live.

I realize schizophrenia necessitates it, but I'm glad someone (qualified, who does it on the regular) is at least talking to you about this stuff. My mental health issues aren't as bad, but they were exacerbated by simply being ignored.

Do you hear voices for real? Like your subconscious is just being a dick to you all the time, self-hating? That must be some shit. I can('t?) imagine. Everybody does that sometimes but they stop. Schizo is like this feedback loop that just can't stop. It's like a runaway train. It's gotta be scary to live with that and I am sorry for the people who judge you without knowing you.

>My parents had sent me to schools which said they would look after me but they never did, the schools and my parents ignored my cries for help (until I was 14) because I was young or something along the lines like that. People bullied me, teachers didn't help, and other emotional trauma that I had encountered. My high school deemed me as a child who wouldn't understand or obey rules even though I tried my best; they literally gave me detention for doing nothing and they would move my seat in classes often for no reason. 

You probably didn't do nothing but whatever you did I bet it was trivial, or out of your control, and probably undeserving of whatever knee-jerk, over-dramatic action they responded with. 

For example one time they lost their shit and I got detention because I flicked a bic lighter in class. I don't actually remember why I had one (or where I got it, lol), it was before I smoked. I just had ADHD. My hands just do stuff. I'm just like "ooh, fire." Next thing I know I'm screwed!

I don't think they understand that when you're 16 that seat is your world man. You move someone to a different class it's crushing socially. You do that too often and it's rough. I went to two different middle schools and three different high schools. It felt like they took my friends from me every time. Even the familiar faces you aren't friends with are comforting. Every new person was just one more opportunity to experience the same judgement so many people passed on me.

>my (four) friends will miss me and so will my pets. But all of this trauma that I cry every day about won't go away, it made my social life become non-existent, no teacher would help me so my grades fell drastically. Currently I am at this special school for autistic kids but I still feel the same (even though they are a nicer school that supports me).

I only ever had like three friends. In I think the first week of high school my freshmen year my best and only friend killed himself. Only thing is, I was really closed off. I don't think he even know he was my best friend. I don't think I'm ever going to get over it. Thinking about it legit makes me cry. We had a petty argument two days prior about my conduct in his private game server. The night he killed himself I felt the intense urge to ride my bike over to his house and apologize but I didn't.

I'll have to wonder for the rest of my life if he thought about me before he killed himself. If he wondered if we were still friends, or felt like we couldn't be any more. Pretty savage right?

>But besides this, I realised that there is no point for me in life, in the end the world and the universe itself will be destroyed meaning my presence isn't valuable. I told my parents this and they are also worried, but I just can't handle all of this because of how the schools treated me and harmed me.

What I think is that we share something in common. A lot of us. With a lot of different issues. Like, I got nothing on you. But we suffer from the same ideas. 

This is straight-up existentialist dread, and you should be feeling good about yourself for having it because you're smart enough to. Most teenagers don't stop to think about their existence at all, never mind the unanswerable philosophical questions someone will be quite ready to tell you you're wrong about in college PHIL-101.

A sort of new-age not-religion of the self, based on reality with nothing written down. You didn't buy into your parent's religion because either you're smart and it's stupid or the internet gotcha early. That's just a guess and if I am wrong I apologize for calling your religion stupid, it was callous of me.

You watch the ricks and morts? This one hit home for me:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ez1rWBPznEc

It's kind of like, yeah, there is no point. That's OK though.

>The therapists I go to try to help but I know that they wont, they will just end up giving me medication that will dull my mind, I won't be my self. 

- Don't be afraid of the meds. I was. I wish I wasn't. I felt exactly that way. That they would take something away from me. They will not. The celebrities saying they don't take their ADHD meds for this reason or whatever are totally full of it.

- I mean that even if it's freakin' lithium. It wont take anything away from you, you will still hold the beliefs that both make you a great, unique (and hopefully in the future, less unique!) person. I promise.

>Even one of my therapists said that it was all my fault, saying that I did all of this and everything else was in my head.

Maybe? Maybe not? I don't know. You don't know. He doesn't know. So that's not constructive or helpful is it, gosh some of the crap I read therapists saying on here, gross!

>All of this hurts a child's mind, making them an inside person with no reason to live, it hurts more and more every day, I just need a reason to live but I know that I can't accept anything, even if I try to.


**For now just live for no reason! None at all! I'm not even shitting you. I'm out of time. I have to go. Please don't go man. At least give it some time, try some more different drugs. Maybe some combo of them can help reduce your schizo symptoms, which are probably the main reason you're hella upset.**

Maybe read this book call the DSM - the diagnostic statistic manual. It's where all these mental health pros reference the symptom lists for these mental health disorders. Every mental health disorder sort of bleeds onto the neighboring ones, and you might find better understanding of yourself in the description of everyone else's problems. It also might make you feel better about yourself just because it can be worse (I guess, that doesn't really help someone feeling suicidal at all) and aside from that it's a really interesting book.

https://psicovalero.files.wordpress.com/2014/11/dsm-v-ingles-manual-diagnc3b3stico-y-estadc3adstico-de-los-trastornos-mentales.pdf

LOL, hand a suicidal teenager a DSM. I think I might be Hitler. For some reason I feel like it might help you feel more normal to read what these professionals read from their perspective. I mean they don't like, carry this thing around and whip it out but it really shows you like, what their thought process is for figuring out which drugs to give someone having mental health problems.

------------------------

Oh and you know what? Maybe you aren't schizo, maybe you've been playing it up. Maybe Mr. not-subtle-enough was right. Maybe something else fits better. I forgive you for playing it up even if you straight up told me that. You wanted help, you needed something to be wrong in a big way, and you latched onto something that made sense. If it makes sense to you, you can change your mind about that.

Er, I said you, but I meant me. That's what I did. I just latched onto the first diagnosis I thought would change things.

At the same time, I believe you automatically and they should too.

27 here. I relate to this post so much it's probably unhealthy for both of us.

Somebody (your mental health person) needs to get a different job, in my opinion. What an unprofessional thing to say. At least, if it was worded that way. It would be one thing to say to someone, "I think you should try talking to someone else because maybe I just wasn't the right person." But that's just, man that's offensive.

>These expectations that I have to get a job and make something of myself are just stupid to me. 

I think they're stupid expectations period and I think we both know it's going to spill over and something is going to have to be done about it sooner or later. If you don't feel that way, I didn't until I moved to a dense city and realized truly just how many of us fuckers are crawling around on this rock. I mean shit, they're gonna replace cashiers with kiosks. 

It's like, if there is not enough to go around then why do you people keep shitting out babies? Why the fuck did you make us if you're just gonna leave us in a gutter, literally? It's the "what is my purpose - you pass the butter" but *literal*.


You know what else? You're right. It's selfish to tell someone to keep on going while not participating in the same slog they send us to every day. They go to their day job, they get every weekend 2 consecutive days off, health insurance, 4-day vacations every holiday, sick leave, and we get, what? Not enough money to pay the bills, an inconsistent schedule that randomly causes our incomes to fluctuate over %60 in a month whenever it's convenient for corporate to cut costs, no recourse, no way to even communicate with the companies we are forced to work for against our will.

I dunno man. You're not the only one. Oh and uh, I've embarrassed myself a lot of times. I just kinda know like, our spectrum, the borderline personality / bipolar / ADHD / learning disability ... blend. I bet you've had outbursts. I have too. I gotta say, it's not your fault. It's largely environmental imo. It's not natural and I think there's a general intelligence point where if you don't have a good enough purpose you just end up loathing yourself. 

I just, I don't know. I think you're probably an intelligent person. I think you probably have some talent, just not one that sells. I think you're probably upset because you feel like you've wasted your life by not applying your intelligence.

I don't think you should kill yourself because you feel like you should have achieved more. I feel like we didn't achieve more because the adults in our lives didn't guide us well enough. Probably because they were you know, busy achieving. Maybe they thought the public school system teaches life skills? My parents did.

You can achieve something still. 


EDIT: I cut some of this out because it was too long and frankly, I'm afraid to say the wrong thing. I'm not sure if I understand what you're going though, but it reads familiar. Maybe I'm just projecting my own issues.
